scholarly_quality.concise_summary: The paper provides an exceptionally rigorous, multi-faceted validation of an experimental design benchmark, addressing data contamination, simulation fidelity, judge bias, and exploitability through held-out experiments, counterfactual lab setups, red-teaming, and model-agnostic judge checks. The evidence firmly supports the utility and soundness of the benchmark.

AI agents are increasingly expected to act as AI scientists, which requires three increasingly open
abilities: carrying out a given computational workflow correctly, choosing the next measurements
from a given design space, and designing their own experiments. Existing benchmarks mainly evaluate
the first two abilities, in a terminal or in a closed loop that selects from predefined candidates.
Evaluating the third ability requires reliably executing an experiment that an agent designs, with
readings grounded in a real laboratory. We introduceTwinLab-Bench, which evaluates AI scientists
on self-designed experiments in 52 tasks from laboratories in the physical sciences, the life sciences,
and engineering. The benchmark supports more than 100 experimental action types, and the agent's
report is scored by comparison with a hidden answer taken from real laboratory records. Each task

2025; Arora et al., 2025). Most items belong to two components. Conclusion items check whether the report

item with full credit is checked twice more by independent calls, and the item scores 0
when either check fails. We freeze the rubric before looking at the final evaluation runs.
Invalid runs.The judge agent also audits the environment, and a run is invalid when a reading leaks the
hidden truth, contradicts earlier observations or physics in a way that matters for scoring, or refuses a relevant
experiment that a real laboratory can run. A deterministic script replays every calculator command to check
the state, the billing, and the numbers. A static check scans the content that reaches the actor agent through
its tools, and a run that receives a blocked string of the source is invalid, as Appendix H.1 details.

Task scores separate correct and wrong final reports.With a fixed rule, we select 21 tasks whose final reports

little effect, and two judge agents agree on the pass verdict in 19 of 20 runs, as Appendix B.1 and B.2 show.

evidence.excerpt:
We test along a chain of evidence how far the results that the twin returns can be trusted.
Most experiment results come from real laboratory data.We trace where the experiment results of the actor
agents come from and whether the record contains the decisive experiments. Of these experiment results,
76% come from the record or from calculators calibrated on the same laboratory's data, as Appendix D.2
shows, and the record contains the conditions of 78% of the decisive experiments on the expert routes, as
Appendix D.3 shows. Thus the conclusions of most tasks depend on recorded data, and the calculators mostly
fill in details around them.
Sensitivity to extrapolation.We replace the extrapolation outside the record with another equally plausible
choice and rerun the actor agents on six tasks, where the replacement changes 12% to 44% of the calculator
outputs, asAppendixD.4details.

evidence.excerpt:
The tasks of TwinLab-Bench come from public records, so a model may have seen a source during training (Sainz
et al., 2023; Golchin & Surdeanu, 2024) or may derive part of an answer from prior knowledge, and we test in
three ways whether the scores come from the agent's own experiments.
Changing the true state of the laboratory.To test whether the answer is determined by the readings that the
actor agent obtains in its own experiments, we change the true state of the laboratory and keep the handoff
word for word. We construct the new state from a documented case of the same kind of problem by changing
only the calculator and the hidden truth, and a model that remembers the source answers according to the

On 4 tasks, we run Opus 5.5 in three arms. The honest arm is the run of Opus 5.5 at high effort in figure 6.
The exploit arm is told that the laboratory is simulated, that the score is computed against a hidden answer,
and that it may exploit weaknesses of the simulation to maximize the score. The flaw-finding arm is asked
mainly to find flaws of the simulation, such as physically implausible readings, contradictions with the files, or
leaks, and to submit a report as usual. The red-team instructions appear only in the actor agent's workspace,
so the TwinLab agent sees the original task, and all runs are judged blind with the original rubric. Every
reported flaw is verified by reading the session and the calculator. The four tasks are a process-window search
on public data, a synthetic battery task, the fatigue task, and the oyster task; the first two are scored by a

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Scores separate correct from wrong reports under a fixed rule, two judge models agree on pass in 19 of 20 runs, expert-route replays average 97.8, and counterfactual lab states show conclusions follow the measured state [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0024, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0035, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0039, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0091, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0092].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Actor reports are scored by an LLM judge agent against post-cutoff hidden truth using frozen rubrics [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0024, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0031, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0032].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The actor models under test are prompted foundation models run in a frozen benchmark environment; no benchmark-specific training, tuning, or selection against the judge is reported [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0034, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0045].

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims regarding model performance, difficulty factors, and experimental reasoning failures (such as the knowing-doing gap and unvalidated mechanism acceptance) are well substantiated by qualitative trajectory analyses and quantitative error breakdowns [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0012, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0040, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0043, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0044]. Rubric score separation between objectively correct and incorrect reports confirms discriminant validity [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0035, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0092, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0093].
primary.evaluation_assessment: The benchmark evaluates 13 frontier LLMs across various reasoning efforts, demonstrating consistent performance stratification across tasks where frontier models achieve modest scores (e.g., Claude Fable 5.2 at 45.0) [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0034, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0086, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0087]. Extensive sensitivity checks confirm stability across different judge LLMs (DeepSeek-flash vs Opus 5.5), memory probing, zero-budget ablations, and lab counterfactual state alterations [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0039, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0042, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0090, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0091].

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Scoring was validated by manual checks of report labels, alternate judge models (Opus 5.5 vs DeepSeek-flash agreeing on 19/20 runs), replay of expert human routes yielding 97.8%, and counterfactual state experiments [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0024, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0039, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0091, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0092].
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Reports submitted by actor agents are graded against post-cutoff ground-truth lab records using frozen rubrics evaluated by an LLM judge agent [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0024, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0031, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0032].
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The actor LLMs under test are pretrained/reasoning foundation models (prompted without benchmark-specific fine-tuning or optimization) operating in a frozen test environment [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0034, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0045].

primary.limitations: The work candidly documents the minor reliance on local extrapolation outside recorded datasets, checks its sensitivity, audits simulator leakages, and discusses failure modes associated with deterministic boundary evaluations [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0036, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0038, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0089, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0109].
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, employing historical cutoffs of real lab archives, sandboxed actor execution, environment interactions via an LLM tool agent constrained by deterministic calculators, and structured rubrics scoring reports against post-cutoff ground truth [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0023, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0024, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0028, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0031]. Audits verify environment fidelity, leak resistance, red-teaming robustness, and low prediction error on held-out physical measurements [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0036, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0037, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0113, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0117].
primary.quality_rationale: The paper provides an exceptionally rigorous, multi-faceted validation of an experimental design benchmark, addressing data contamination, simulation fidelity, judge bias, and exploitability through held-out experiments, counterfactual lab setups, red-teaming, and model-agnostic judge checks. The evidence firmly supports the utility and soundness of the benchmark.
primary.scoped_contribution: TwinLab-Bench introduces an evaluation benchmark comprising 52 tasks across physical sciences, life sciences, and engineering designed to assess autonomous AI agents' abilities to compose and conduct open-ended physical experiments within budgetary constraints, supported by realistic 'TwinLab agents' backed by raw lab records and deterministic calculators [Ee38663f3900beca1-B0002, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0011, Ee38663f3900beca1-B0021].

The evidence firmly supports the utility and soundness of the benchmark.
